newsitem.title: UK: Hamleys profits up, shares fall as chief quits.
newsitem.headline: Hamleys profits up, shares fall as chief quits.

text.p: Hamleys, the toy retailer famous for its giant store on London's Regent Street, on Thursday reported an 18 percent jump in profits but saw its shares fall on news the chief executive had quit after only five months.

Profits in the half year to July 27 rose to two million pounds from 1.7 million pounds ($2.66 million) on sales up four percent to 11.4 million from 11.0 million. The dividend was three pence a share.
The group said chief executive Geoff Cullinan had resigned to pursue other business interests, but would stay on while Hamleys looked for a replacement.
Chairman Howard Dyer said the group, which had traded for the last five years without a chief executive, appointed Cullinan to help develop the business.
"He came from a consulting background where he focused on retailing and has decided really that perhaps it was not for him," Dyer told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Cullinan, whose salary was in excess of 100,000 pounds, will leave with a "package", but Dyer would not give details.
Retail analysts said they thought the shares, which fell seven pence to 365-1/2, had overreacted as Hamleys' business was performing well and cashflow was strong.
"The reaction is overdone as the underlying business is strong as normal," said retail analyst Amit Thakar at ABM-AMRO Hoare Govett.
The group is expanding overseas and has just opened a Hamleys store in Singapore Airport. It is also opening franchises in Saudi Arabia, with the first one due to open by the middle of next year.
There are already branches at Heathrow and Schipol airports and the Channel tunnel, as well as House of Toys concessions in House of Fraser shops. ($1=.6388 Pound)
